question: Should OpenClaw expose current-session compaction as a model-callable `session_status(action: "compact")` mutation, or require a different policy/API boundary?
rationale: The code path is narrow and well-proven, but it intentionally lets a model-originated tool call abort, compact, and resume active session state without an authorized sender command; automation cannot decide that trust boundary.

options.title: Approve Narrow Current-Session Action
options.body: Refresh the branch, keep the current-session-only checks, and approve this limited model-callable compaction boundary before merge.

options.title: Require An Explicit Policy Gate
options.body: Keep the implementation shape but expose it only behind a maintainer-approved tool policy or config gate.

options.title: Defer To Broader Continuation Work
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers want self-compaction to ship only as part of the broader continuation API.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow Current-Session Action
recommendation.body: Refresh the branch, keep the current-session-only checks, and approve this limited model-callable compaction boundary before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked issue already has maintainer follow-up framing from this person, and recent history shows adjacent session-status/docs involvement.
